verdicts.rationale: Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors build directly on the standard error concept by adjusting it for cases where the standard deviation of the error term varies across observations.
Heteroskedasticity is a specific condition regarding the variance of the error term depending on the regressors, directly extending the basic concept of variance.
Weighted least squares uses the inverse of error variance to weight observations, directly applying the concept of variance to improve estimation efficiency.
Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors rely on asymptotic normality justified by the central limit theorem to ensure valid statistical inference.
Heteroskedasticity describes errors with non-constant variance, serving as the direct opposition to homoskedasticity where error variance is constant.
The Breusch-Pagan test checks joint significance by using an auxiliary F-test or LM test, applying joint coefficient testing principles to heteroskedasticity.
Both are diagnostic tests for regression residuals, with the Breusch-Pagan test checking for heteroskedasticity and the Durbin-Watson test checking for autocorrelation.
